_description: Fault traces, dips and down-dip geometry used to imprint fault damage zones on the NW Himalaya tomography model. Coordinates are [lon, lat] (WGS84). Each dip_profile entry is [depth_top_km, dip_deg]: the fault dips at dip_deg from depth_top_km down to the next entry (or to max_depth_km). Traces may be given in any order; the script orients them so that the fault dips towards dip_azimuth_deg.

_notes.vs_reduction_vs_depth: [depth_km, Vs reduction %] pairs, linearly interpolated, last value held below. Default: 10% at the surface (down to 5 km), easing to 5% at 20 km, so damage is strongest in the shallow brittle crust. Use [[0,10]] for a uniform 10% along the whole fault plane.
_notes.vp_reduction_ratio: Vp reduction as a fraction of the Vs reduction (0 = Vp unchanged, 1 = same % as Vs).
_notes.rho_reduction_ratio: Density reduction as a fraction of the Vs reduction (0 = density unchanged).
_notes.damage_zone_half_width_km: Physical half-width of the fault damage zone, measured normal to the fault plane. It is widened where needed so the ~4.1-4.7 km horizontal / 0.5 km vertical tomography grid can resolve the zone (see README).
_notes.taper_width_factor: Outside the core zone the reduction falls to zero with a cosine taper this many core half-widths wide.
_notes.end_taper_km: Along-strike cosine taper beyond the ends of each trace.
_notes.splay_termination_margin_km: Splay thrusts (terminate_at_mht = true) stop where they reach the MHT, plus this margin (they merge into the MHT damage zone there).

faults.name: MFT / Main Himalayan Thrust (MHT)
faults.trace_source: HimaTibetMap (Styron et al., 2010) via the GEM Global Active Faults database (Styron & Pagani, 2020); NW of 75.7E extended by hand along the Siwalik front towards Jammu and joined to the GEM/EMME Salt Range segment.
faults.geometry_note: Frontal ramp ~30 deg to 5 km, flat decollement ~6 deg to ~12 km beneath the Lesser Himalaya (75 km north of the front), mid-crustal ramp ~15 deg to ~20 km beneath the Higher Himalaya, i.e. the down-dip end of the locked MHT that ruptured in 1905. Consistent with balanced sections across the Kangra re-entrant (Powers et al., 1998) and the ramp-flat MHT of Caldwell et al. (2013).

faults.name: Jwalamukhi Thrust (JMT)
faults.trace_source: Approximate, hand-placed from regional maps of the Kangra re-entrant (e.g. Powers et al., 1998; Thakur, 2004).
faults.geometry_note: Listric splay, ~35 deg near surface flattening to ~25 deg, soling into the MHT decollement.

faults.name: Main Boundary Thrust (MBT)
faults.trace_source: Approximate, hand-placed from regional maps (e.g. Thakur, 2004; Yin, 2006): Murree/Riasi thrust near Jammu, Dharamsala, Kalka, Dehradun-Mussoorie, Kathgodam.
faults.geometry_note: Steep (~45 deg) at the surface, listric, soling into the MHT at ~10-12 km depth.

faults.name: Main Central Thrust (MCT)
faults.trace_source: Approximate, hand-placed from regional maps (e.g. Yin, 2006): Kishtwar, north of the Dhauladhar, Kullu, Sutlej valley (Jeori), Bhagirathi (Bhatwari), Alaknanda (Helang).
faults.geometry_note: ~35 deg near surface flattening to ~25 deg, joining the MHT near the top of the mid-crustal ramp.

faults.name: South Tibetan Detachment (STD) / Zanskar Shear Zone
faults.trace_source: Approximate, hand-placed from regional maps (e.g. Yin, 2006).
faults.geometry_note: Low-angle (~25 deg) north-dipping normal-sense detachment, kept to the upper 15 km.

faults.name: Kaurik-Chango Fault
faults.trace_source: HimaTibetMap (Styron et al., 2010) via the GEM Global Active Faults database.
faults.geometry_note: Steep west-dipping normal fault (1975 Kinnaur earthquake), kept to the upper 15 km.

faults.name: Karakoram Fault
faults.trace_source: HimaTibetMap (Styron et al., 2010) via the GEM Global Active Faults database (segment within/near the model).
faults.geometry_note: Near-vertical dextral fault (~80 deg NE), through the seismogenic crust.

references: Caldwell, W. B., et al. (2013). Characterizing the Main Himalayan Thrust in the Garhwal Himalaya, India with receiver function CCP stacking. EPSL 367, 15-27.
Powers, P. M., Lillie, R. J., & Yeats, R. S. (1998). Structure and shortening of the Kangra and Dehra Dun reentrants, Sub-Himalaya, India. GSA Bulletin 110, 1010-1027.
Styron, R., Taylor, M., & Okoronkwo, K. (2010). Database of active structures from the Indo-Asian collision. Eos 91(20), 181-182.
Styron, R., & Pagani, M. (2020). The GEM Global Active Faults Database. Earthquake Spectra 36(1_suppl), 160-180.
Thakur, V. C. (2004). Active tectonics of Himalayan Frontal Thrust and seismic hazard to Ganga Plain. Current Science 86(11), 1554-1560.

Yin, A. (2006). Cenozoic tectonic evolution of the Himalayan orogen as constrained by along-strike variation of structural geometry, exhumation history, and foreland sedimentation. Earth-Science Reviews 76, 1-131.
